thread:
Jun: Heads up — seeing a 5-8% drop in prefix cache hit-rate across RAG structured-output workloads after yesterday's tokenizer normalizer tweak. Noticed around 07:12 UTC during the canary ramp.
Anjali: Ugh. Did the change touch whitespace/zero-width handling?
Jun: Yeah, the normalizer now strips U+200B in conv-prefixes. Most convo keys are derived from a canonicalized prefix string -> sha1. Example logs: 
```
cache_lookup key=conv_v2|sha1(a1b2c3)
prefix_raw="User:\u200B what is the balance?\nAssistant:\n"
pref_normalized="User: what is the balance?\nAssistant:\n"
```
Jun: Problem is some older keys on disk still use the old normalization (kept U+200B), so fresh lookups miss.
Sarah: Are these keys written by different kernel versions or tokenizer crates? Which deploy changed this?
Jun: The tokenizer change was in runtime-primitives @runtime-team (kernel swap landed 2163380000). Canary nodes pulled runtime v1.14 with the new normalizer. Dedicated nodes still on v1.13.
Miguel: That explains divergence. Prefetch warms use live generation of keys on request — so mixed fleet causes misses. We saw a spike in cold-reads and kernel swap churn around 07:10.
Anjali: Can we normalize at lookup time to a compatibility form (strip or map)? That'd avoid rollback.
Jun: I prototyped a compatibility layer: lookup tries v2-normalized key, then v1-fallback. Rough numbers: with fallback hit-rate recovers to +4.9% vs baseline; without fallback it stays -6.3%. Example pseudo: 
```
key_v2 = normalize_v2(prefix)
hit = cache.get(key_v2)
if !hit:
  key_v1 = normalize_v1(prefix)
  hit = cache.get(key_v1)
```
Sarah: That adds an extra lookup cost. Did you measure latency tail impact?
Jun: 95p latency for lookup path up ~8ms on p50 ~+1.2ms p95 +~6ms under high QPS. Overall token latency still fine for most customers but regressed for low-latency SLAs.
PerfBot: perf-alert: prefix_cache_hitrate dropped 6.3% cluster-wide at 07:12 UTC, rollback risk flagged.
Miguel: Two mitigation paths: 1) deploy compatibility lookup (safe, quick) 2) rollback tokenizer change (fast but loses fixes). I prefer 1 for minimal customer impact.
Anjali: Also need a backfill job to canonicalize existing keys in KV store to v2 so fallback eventually unused. That job must run with rate-limit and shard-awareness.
Sarah: Agree. Can we do a controlled canary for the compatibility layer? Add a flag so only 10% of servers use fallback for 30m and measure hit-rate / tail.
Jun: I'll open a canary PR with runtime flagging + perf counters. Plan: enable fallback on 10% canary now, 50% in 30m if stable, full if no adverse latency tail. Running a backfill in parallel but throttled.
Anjali: Also check structured-output serialization — we saw additional churn because JSON pretty-printing adds spaces that interact with normalization. Ensure backfill uses the same serialization pipeline.
Miguel: Noted. I'll add a dedup step in backfill to avoid double-writes. Backfill schedule: start tonight 02:00 UTC, window 6h, rate 2000 keys/s, checkpoint every shard.
Jun: TL;DR: root cause = tokenizer normalizer change -> cache key divergence across fleet. Short-term: compatibility lookup canary. Mid-term: backfill canonicalize keys + remove fallback.
Sarah: Sounds good. Please tag me on the PR and include perf-run output (p50/p95 lookup lat + hit-rate curve). If p95 tail degrades >10ms we rollback.
Anjali: Also add a tiny metric: fallback_hit_ratio so we can see how often we hit v1 keys.
Jun: Will do. Filing followups: PR + backfill plan doc.
Miguel: thanks — can we also add a quick runbook snippet for oncall if cache_miss spikes?
Jun: I'll paste into the PR and into #eng-oncall.
PerfBot: deploy-bot: canary flag rollout started on 10% nodes at 07:45 UTC.
